transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm here because... things at the office have been really weird. What really made me come in is that I just can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking my buys. Like, they're actively messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. 

And vendors are just... you know, they're sketchy. Like this one guy who sells us bulk energy drinks. I used to drink those all the time back in high school, actually. The blue kind, not the red ones, because the red ones taste exactly like cherry cough syrup. We took a whole cooler of the blue ones down to the lake for senior skip day... man, the water was freezing that year. We didn't even end up swimming, just sat on the tailgate of my buddy's truck. 

But anyway, yeah, my supervisor keeps pulling up all these reports to show me that the numbers don't prove anything is being messed with, but I know what's going on. I mean, you can't even trust computers half the time anyway, right? My friend downloaded a spreadsheet for his fantasy football draft last week and it completely fried his hard drive. Just totally gone. So yeah, that's why I'm here.
Do you feel that people at work are deliberately acting against you or trying to harm you in some way?

Yeah, exactly, like I was just saying. They are absolutely doing it on purpose. It's not an accident that my buys are being tracked and the launch numbers get screwed up just to make me look like an idiot. 

And Dave—my supervisor—he just points at his little printed reports and says there's no proof, but he's completely blind to it. He always prints those reports out on that really thick paper, you know, the heavy glossy kind? We get that paper from a supplier out in Ohio. I actually drove through Ohio once on a road trip with my older brother right after I graduated. We stopped at this middle-of-nowhere diner that had the biggest pancakes I've ever seen in my life, like, literally the size of a hubcap. My brother tried to eat three of them and ended up throwing up behind a gas station. 

But yeah, Dave just doesn't see what they're actually doing with the numbers right in front of him.
Do you ever feel like you have special powers, a unique role, or that you're meant to do something extraordinary that other people aren't aware of?

Well, yeah, actually. Sometimes I just... I get this absolute clarity. I start believing I can spot the next big trend before anyone out in L.A. even has a clue. It's like the entire sneaker market is basically just waiting on my decisions, which is wild because, technically, I'm still just one of the junior buyers. But I know they're waiting on me. 

Sneakers are just crazy right now, anyway. My buddy actually moved out to L.A. last year to try and do the whole influencer thing with streetwear. He bought this ridiculously expensive camera, one of those Sony ones with the huge lenses. I told him he should just use his phone, because honestly, phone cameras are insane now. I dropped my phone in a puddle outside a concert like three months ago, and it sat there for a solid ten minutes before I realized, and it still works perfectly. We were seeing this underground indie band... man, the bass was so loud my teeth were literally vibrating. I couldn't hear right for two days. 

But yeah, I just... I know what's going to hit the market before anyone else does.
Do you believe that random events, like things happening in the world or actions other people take, are specifically connected to you or influenced by you?

No, not really. I mean, random stuff is just... random. It just happens. I definitely don't think I'm controlling the news or whatever people are doing out there. I don't even really watch the news anyway, mostly I just watch sports highlights or random stuff on YouTube. 

YouTube's algorithm is getting so weird lately, though. Like, last week I watched exactly one video about fixing a leaky faucet because the sink in my apartment was dripping. It was doing that annoying drip all night, and my landlord is this older guy who literally takes weeks to come fix anything. He drives this ancient Buick that smells exactly like peppermint and stale cigarettes. I don't even know where you buy those specific peppermint candies anymore, you know the ones with the little red and white swirls wrapped in that crinkly plastic? My grandma used to keep those in a heavy glass bowl on her coffee table, right next to these weird ceramic frogs she collected. She had like fifty of them, all different sizes. 

But... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, world events and stuff. Yeah, no, I don't think any of that is connected to me.
Have you ever seen, heard, or felt things that others around you don't seem to notice?

Yeah, actually... it happens mostly when I'm alone. Like, sometimes when I'm in the stockroom pulling inventory, or driving back from a vendor meeting, I'll hear this guy's voice. It sounds like he's right behind me, right over my shoulder, and he'll say stuff like, 'Move faster, Scott,' or he'll just start laughing at the shoes I picked out. But every time I turn around, there's absolutely nobody there. 

It's really freaky in the stockroom because that place is huge and echoes a lot. We just got these new fluorescent lights installed back there because the old ones kept buzzing. I hate that buzzing sound. It reminds me of the neon sign outside this pizza place I used to work at in high school. The sign was supposed to say 'Luigi's,' but the 'L' and the 'U' were burnt out, so it just said 'igi's' for like two years. We had this delivery driver there, Mike, who drove a completely rusted-out Honda Civic, but he put these massive spinning rims on it. It looked ridiculous. He actually got pulled over once because one of the rims flew off on the highway and hit a state trooper's cruiser. He got fired the next day, which sucked because he was the only one who knew how to fix the dough mixer when it jammed. 

But yeah, I hear that guy's voice, and nobody else is ever around when it happens.
Do you believe that you are more important, more powerful, or have abilities that other people don't?

Well, I think I kind of mentioned this earlier, but yeah, I definitely have moments where I just know things. Like, I start believing I can spot the next trend before anyone in L.A. even has a clue. It's like the whole sneaker market is basically waiting on my decisions, which is crazy because, you know, I'm still one of the junior buyers. 

But it's just this feeling of absolute certainty. Speaking of junior buyers, the guy they hired right after me, Kevin, he is completely useless. I don't know how he even got the job. He wears these awful square-toed dress shoes to work, which is literally a sin in the footwear industry. I told him once he needed to upgrade, and he said he buys all his clothes at this discount warehouse out by the interstate. That place is so depressing, it's right next to this abandoned bowling alley. I used to go bowling there for birthday parties when I was a kid. They had this arcade game, one of those claw machines, but the claw was completely rigged. You could never grab anything. I spent like twenty bucks trying to win this stuffed alien toy once, and it just kept slipping right through the prongs. My mom was so mad I spent all my allowance on it. She made me do extra chores for a week, mostly weeding the garden, which I hated because we had these massive thorny bushes... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about being important. Yeah, I just... I know the market needs my eye.

Delusional disorder, grandiose type, is the most fitting diagnosis based on the clinical information provided so far.
